hints: Focus on the shape around each central atom, since bond angle is decided by electron pair geometry, not just the formula.
Draw C2H4 as planar with a C=C double bond, so each carbon has 3 bonding regions and no lone pair.
Compare PF5 with its 5 bonding pairs to NCl3 with its lone pair, and ask which geometries actually include a 120 degree angle.
walkthrough:
**Recall how shape controls angle**

Think side by side with me. Electron pairs repel to get as far apart as possible. That arrangement fixes the bond angle.

Rule to use:
$$\text{shape from electron pairs} \rightarrow \text{bond angle}$$

**Check molecule 1, C2H4**

Each carbon in ethene has 3 sigma bonding regions and no lone pair. That gives trigonal planar geometry around each C.

Shape:
$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_4 \text{ : trigonal planar at each C, angle } \approx 120^{\circ}$$

**Check molecule 2, PF5**

Phosphorus has 5 bonding pairs and no lone pair. That gives trigonal bipyramidal geometry.

Shape:
$$\text{PF}_5 \text{ : trigonal bipyramidal, angles } 90^{\circ}, 120^{\circ} \text{ and } 180^{\circ}$$
So the three equatorial P-F bonds are 120 degrees apart. This one counts.

**Check molecule 3, NCl3**

Nitrogen has 3 bonding pairs plus 1 lone pair. That gives trigonal pyramidal shape, like ammonia.

Shape:
$$\text{NCl}_3 \text{ : pyramidal, angle } \approx 107^{\circ}$$
The lone pair squeezes the angle below 109.5 degrees, so there is no 120 degree angle. This one does not count.

**Combine the conclusion**

Molecules 1 and 2 contain a 120 degree angle, molecule 3 does not. That matches the 1 and 2 only combination.

options.A: This means 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. It is wrong because NCl3 is pyramidal with an angle near 107 degrees due to its lone pair, so it has no 120 degree angle.
options.B: This means 1 and 2 only are correct. C2H4 is trigonal planar at each carbon with about 120 degrees, and PF5 is trigonal bipyramidal with 120 degrees between equatorial bonds. NCl3 is correctly excluded.
options.C: This means 2 and 3 only are correct. It correctly includes PF5 but wrongly includes NCl3 and wrongly excludes C2H4. NCl3 has about 107 degrees, not 120 degrees.
options.D: This means 1 only is correct. It correctly includes C2H4 but wrongly leaves out PF5. Students choose this if they forget that trigonal bipyramidal also contains 120 degree equatorial angles.
